title: Dynamic Rebatching for Efficient Early-Exit Inference with DREX
technique: Early-exit LLM serving: dynamic rebatching at each exit ramp with copy-free buffer, profitability-aware adaptive rebatching threshold, SLA-aware scheduler, state-copying for skipped-layer KV

optimized_metrics.evidence: We further introduce two novel mechanisms to ensure throughput gain and SLA compliance despite the remaining overheads
DREX completely eliminates involuntary exits, providing a key guarantee for preserving the output quality intended by the EE mechanism.

SLA-aware forced flushing (§5.3): if requests' SLA deadlines approach without the system accumulating a sufficient number of requests ... ; Incorporating age and SLA: To prevent starvation and improve SLA adherence, we consider the expected completion time and SLA of the requests

headline_claim.text: DREX improves throughput by 2-12% compared to baseline approaches while maintaining output quality. Crucially, DREX completely eliminates involuntary exits

reported_metrics.where: Fig 8 P95 confidence score; Fig 10 BERT score
Fig 4, §7.4 KV cache size / memory copies

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Throughput: Total number of output tokens generated per second.
metric_definitions.notes: Output tokens only; single node, not per GPU.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: RCT: Time between when a request is scheduled to when it is complete.
metric_definitions.notes: Measured from scheduling, so excludes queueing before scheduling.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Confidence score: Softmax confidence scores of the EE tokens, indicating the model's certainty and output quality.
metric_definitions.notes: Proxy quality metric; P95 of this score used (lower tail).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: BERT Score [50]: Measures the semantic similarity between the generated summary and the reference summary. A higher score indicates better quality.
Involuntary Exit: Percentage of tokens that were forced to exit, despite not meeting their individual confidence threshold.
Involuntary Stay: Percentage of tokens that were forced to continue, despite meeting their individual confidence threshold to exit.

slo_spec: SLA expressed as request completion time (RCT) requirement converted to iterations; scheduler uses r_SLA minus expected remaining; 'SLA pressure' parameter 0-1 sweep
load_regime: Offline batch evaluation at fixed batch sizes (e.g., 1, 8 and others) on CNN/DM summarization; SLA-pressure sweep for RCT; no open-loop arrival-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: With no SLA pressure, throughput +11.4% over Consensus but avg RCT 1.4x and tail RCT 3x worse; SLA-aware scheduling raises avg RCT by up to 58.4% relative trade for throughput. Greedy policy gets highest throughput at 96% worse P95 confidence.
hardware: NVIDIA GPUs incl. H200 node (141GB) for 70B
extractor_notes: QUALITY recorded as constraint (zero involuntary exits is a guarantee), but quality is measured by proxy (softmax confidence and BERTScore), not task accuracy. Throughput gain is modest and measured offline at fixed batch size. Early-exit is not speculative decoding; layer value assigned for closest fit.

tail_audit.metrics: request completion time (RCT) average and P95 (reported); SLA is per-request deadline

load_class_quote: Rebatching improves throughput by as much as 12% compared to non-EE ... batch size of 8, and the lower portion a batch size of 4 (Fig 8/10 captions); fixed batch sizes on CNN/DM, no arrival process
